newsitem.title: USA: AccuMed backs analysts' breakeven view.
newsitem.headline: AccuMed backs analysts' breakeven view.

text.p: AccuMed International Inc said Tuesday it backs analysts' estimates of breakeven results by the 1997 fourth quarter.

"We are comfortable with analysts' estimates that we will reach break-even or be profitable by the fourth quarter of this year," said Peter Gombrich, chairman and chief executive. "The company should show significant revenue growth for the remainder of 1997," he said in a statement.
Earlier, AccuMed reported a 1997 first quarter loss of $2.6 million or $0.12 a share, before a non-recurring, non-cash writeoff of $3.6 million or $0.17 a share.
This compares with a loss of $2.6 million or $0.17 for the first quarter in 1996. First quarter earnings are based on about 21 million shares compared with 15.8 million in 1996.

The 1996 first quarter results also included a net charge of $1.0 million or $0.06 consisting of a writeoff of $3.5 million of acquired in-process research and development costs offset by recognition of $2.5 million in license income.

"The ESP Culture System II product line acquisition completed at the beginning of March 1997 has performed better than planned since acquired by AccuMed," he said. This product line, which had 1996 revenues of more than $16 million will be a key profit and revenue contributor to the results of the Microbiology division, he added.
In other developments, AccuMed said it received and responded to a list of questions from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration regarding its application to market its TracCell slide mapping system.
AccuMed said it met directly with the FDA in conjunction with its reply to the questions and continues to be optimistic that it will soon get FDA marketing clearance for the device.
AccuMed develops diagnostic products which screen cell specimens.
